title: Sign-problem-resilient singular-value probe in determinant quantum Monte Carlo
abstract: The sign problem limits determinant quantum Monte Carlo studies of strongly correlated fermion systems. In the spin-channel Hubbard-Stratonovich decoupling, spin correlations are exactly related to auxiliary-field correlations. This relation implies that an antiferromagnetic transition reorganizes auxiliary-field configurations and thereby changes the statistical structure of the resulting fermion matrices. We use the adjacent gap ratio of low-lying singular values of the space-time fermion matrix to probe interaction-driven transitions in two half-filled honeycomb-lattice Hubbard models. In the sign-free honeycomb Hubbard model, the statistic tracks the established transition from a Dirac semimetal to an antiferromagnetic Mott insulator. In the complex-weight Haldane-Hubbard model, the transition-sensitive feature remains visible in the phase-quenched reference ensemble and occurs near previous estimates of the transition. Moreover, phase reweighting only weakly modifies the gap ratio over the regimes investigated, despite the rapid suppression of the average phase. These results establish singular-value statistics as a sign-problem-resilient probe of interaction-driven transitions in determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
summary: This work introduces the adjacent gap ratio of singular values of the fermion matrix as a robust diagnostic for phase transitions in DQMC simulations. By analyzing Hubbard models, the authors demonstrate that this spectral statistic remains sensitive to underlying physics even when the simulation encounters a sign or phase problem. This establishes a powerful, sign-problem-resilient probe for strongly correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The sign problem limits the use of determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) for studying strongly correlated fermion systems, necessitating a sign-problem-resilient diagnostic for phase transitions.
main_result: The adjacent gap ratio of low-lying singular values of the space-time fermion matrix successfully tracks interaction-driven phase transitions in both sign-free and complex-weight Hubbard models, remaining robust against phase reweighting.
method: The authors use the adjacent gap ratio of low-lying singular values ($	ext{err}$) of the space-time fermion matrix, derived from the Hubbard-Stratonovich decoupling, as a diagnostic tool.
model_or_system: The study focuses on half-filled honeycomb-lattice Hubbard models, including the sign-free and complex-weight Haldane-Hubbard models, analyzed via DQMC simulations.

important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U/t_1$), lattice geometry (honeycomb), and the auxiliary-field coupling strength ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the local spectral correlations of singular values, which are assumed to be insensitive to the sign/phase of the determinant itself.

paper_structure: The paper develops the diagnostic using the gap ratio, applies it to the honeycomb and Haldane-Hubbard models to demonstrate transition tracking, and contrasts this spin-channel response with an SU(2) charge-channel decomposition to validate the specificity of the spin-based probe.
why_interesting: The technique provides a powerful, purely spectral diagnostic tool that bypasses the fundamental sign problem inherent in simulating fermionic quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding correlated materials.
